verification.note: Fresh selected primary reading of printed705,718–719and723–724 with surrounding Nero/imperial-subjectivation discussion. Veyne uses Foucault’s last two books on self-government and his understanding of power as conducting conduct. This witnesses a specific historical analytical use, not a friendship-based inference or a claim that every part of Veyne’s earlier writing was Foucauldian.
